newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Lee not optimistic on China succession.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Lee not optimistic on China succession.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui said on Friday that he was "not optimistic" about the succession of Chinese President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

"President Lee said he was not optimistic about Jiang Zemin's firm position for succession after Deng Xiaoping died," state-run television quoted Lee as telling a group of senior local newspaper executives.

"President Lee also said he is not optimistic about the 15th (Communist Party) congress," the television quoted Lee as saying, without elaborating. China is due to hold the crucial congress in October.

Lee said earlier on Friday that his government would continue to promote ties with China and predicted Taiwan-China talks would be reopened after Jiang consolidated his power during the party congress.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949. Both governments say they want reunification but under very different terms.
Deng died in Beijing late on Wednesday. Taiwan officials, including Lee, have urged people of the island not to overreact to Deng's death and stay calm.
